title: processkit-cli `inspect --json` output
description: The machine-readable output of `processkit-cli inspect --json`, in both its forms: the single-target snapshot (`--run-id <id> --json`, one JSON object) and the aggregate report (`--all --json`, one JSON array with one entry per snapshot target). Validate against `#/$defs/snapshot` or `#/$defs/inspectAllReport` directly when the invocation is known. Without `--json` both forms print a human-readable rendering instead, which is not a machine contract and is not described here. The normative prose is docs/control-plane.md, "`inspect`" and "The inspect snapshot"; the in-code source of truth is src/control/mod.rs. Validated against fixtures/schema/cli/inspect.jsonl, and against the real binary's output, by tests/machine_output.rs.

rfc3339Millis.description: RFC 3339 UTC with millisecond precision (`…Z`) — the same formatter the JSONL events and the registry record use.

member.description: One member of the run's container, enriched with `ppid`/`name`/`start_time` wherever ProcessKit's members_info() can report them — the same shape, read through the same call, as the JSONL `members_snapshot` (docs/schema.md, "Enriched member fields"). Each enriched field stays independently null where the platform cannot report it.

ppid.description: Parent pid; null where the platform can't report it.

name.description: Executable name; null where the platform can't report it.

start_time.description: Opaque, platform-specific start-time token as a decimal string (not a timestamp); null where the platform can't report it.

snapshot.description: One live run's state, as `inspect --run-id <id> --json` prints it and as the runner replies to the control-plane `inspect` verb. Queried at request time, so it reflects the container's composition *when inspected*, not at start.

snapshot_version.description: Snapshot format version (src/control/mod.rs, SNAPSHOT_VERSION) — the control plane's own client/runner axis, independent of the JSONL `schema_version` and the `registry_version`. Pinned here: a bump is a breaking change to this shape and updates this document with it. The client acts on the value it receives over the wire: a snapshot declaring any other version is refused with CONTROL (103) rather than rendered, so this field can only ever hold the pinned value on stdout (docs/control-plane.md, 'Snapshot version: a foreign version is refused, never rendered').

run_id.description: The run's identifier — the key the client matched in the registry. Never a PID.

mechanism.description: Containment mechanism, in the same vocabulary as the JSONL `run_started`.

root_pid.description: The root child's PID; null if the backend exposed none.

jsonl.description: Absolute path to the run's JSONL lifecycle stream. A runner of this snapshot_version always publishes it; the type stays nullable because the client's parser defaults a missing field to null instead of failing the whole reply. It is not how an older contract's snapshot is read — that one is refused before rendering.

capture_dir.description: Absolute output-capture directory, or null when capture is disabled.

members.description: A point-in-time snapshot of the container's members.

inspectAllReport.description: `inspect --all --json`'s report: exactly one entry per target in the registry snapshot taken when the invocation started — no entry is ever skipped silently. An empty confirmed-live snapshot prints `[]` and exits 0; any `failed` entry makes the whole command exit CONTROL (103) *after* printing the complete report.

run_id.description: The target record's run id. Descriptive only: aggregate dispatch is keyed by the unique registry-record path, so two live records sharing an id are still addressed independently.

status.description: `inspected` — a snapshot was taken; `already_gone` — the target finished before its turn (not an error); `failed` — the still-potentially-live target could not be reached or answered unusably.

snapshot.description: The target's snapshot for `inspected`, null otherwise.

error.description: Why a `failed` target could not be inspected; null for both successful statuses.
